chapter_theme: The nine states and their nine presiding selves (ஒன்பான் அவத்தை, ஒன்பான் அபிமானி): waking, dream and sleep, each taken at three levels, have each a presiding self; passing through them, cut from mala and the gunas, the soul reaches turiya as its true form, and to become Siva beyond the three turiyas is the attainment of Siddhanta.
structure_note: 2537 names the nine presiding selves; 2538 and 2539 describe passing beyond the nine states; 2540 and 2543 count tattvas; 2541, 2542 and 2544 turn to the Lord who orders states, worlds and births; 2545 sums up.

2537.reading: Under the first word are Visva, Taijasa and Prajna; under the good word Virat, Hiranyagarbha and Avyakrita; under the last word the one called Ojita(?), Prajapatya and Visanta: these are the presiding selves.
2537.nuance: தொற்பதம், நற்பதம், பிற்பதம் are taken as the three words of 'tat tvam asi' (tvam, tat, asi). Visva, Taijasa and Prajna are the Vedantic selves of waking, dream and sleep, Virat, Hiranyagarbha and Avyakrita their cosmic counterparts; the third group's names are garbled and the reading is a guess.

2538.reading: When the nine states beginning with waking are let go, unattached to the birth-bound malas and gunas, in the common ground of penance, truth and knowledge the twofold turiya becomes the true form.
2538.nuance: பற்றில் may be 'if one holds' or 'when one releases'; the reading follows the second. துவமார் துரியம் (twofold turiya?) and சொருபம் (svarupa, true form) are technical and unclear.

2539.reading: In a mind become Siva, the self as jiva breaks up and the three birth-bound malas scatter and are uprooted; at the end of the nine, good Siva-knowledge takes their place, and the self becomes itself and not itself.
2539.nuance: சீவன் சிதைய (the jiva breaks up) is the end of the bound self, not of the soul. தான் அல்லவாகுமே may be the soul being neither itself nor other than Siva, the Siddhanta 'not one, not two'. தவமான மவை is obscure.

2540.reading: Before the nine already told there are tattvas, and nine others not to be counted in his word; these two nines can be told later, and setting them aside, the one who rules his own doing excels.
2540.nuance: Which two sets of nine are meant is not said. The last line may praise the Lord as sovereign over his acts or the knower who is master of himself.

2541.reading: Seeking the nature of the Lord who spoke the nine and the five and the world, I say 'my Lord' within, night and day, and he cut away the strong karma and removed it.
2541.nuance: ஒன்பதும் ஐந்தும் may be the nine states and five states, or fourteen worlds. The plain claim is that constant inward remembrance of the Lord cuts karma.

2542.reading: Over many long ages he gathered goods; with many clans and colours and marks he joins; with many fruits and twelve times he thinks; with many lands and ways, he is the one whose nature is in them.
2542.nuance: The verse is a list of manifolds (பல, many, in every line) of which the Lord is the nature. பன்னிரு காலம் (twelve times) may be the twelve months or twelve breaths; much of the verse cannot be fixed.

2543.reading: The first Parapara becomes Parapara the Shakti; light, the Supreme, the soul and the good tattva that is spoken, maya and the two, and release: with the nine distinctions in order, he is the first.
2543.nuance: The verse seems to list nine grades from Siva and Shakti down through soul and maya. Line 3 (ஓதுங் கமைமாயே யோரிரண் டோ ரமுத்தி) is corrupt, and the count cannot be checked.

2544.reading: Making the unclear mind clear, he set by grace for souls hell and heaven, not different from the earth, and endless births; those who do not see clearly what is separate are the souls that took on karma.
2544.nuance: The verse makes even hell and births the work of grace, set for the soul's clarifying, a Siddhanta claim. வேறாத (not different) and வேறாத் தெளியார் (who do not see as separate) play on one word and admit several readings.

2545.reading: In the nine states are the nine presiding selves, with the nine tattvas practised in good measure; to pass beyond the three turiyas that stand in the nine and become Siva in the fair part is the attainment of Siddhanta.
2545.nuance: முத்துரியம் (three turiyas) is taken as the turiya of each of the three levels in 2537. செம்பால் (the fair part) may mean rightly, or in the red (Shakti's) part.

links.note: 2537 only names the nine presiding selves; 2545 sets them in the nine states and makes passing beyond their three turiyas into Siva the goal.

Both verses end on the same words, துவமார் துரியம் சொரூபம், reached in a தவமான சத்திய ஞான state once the birth-bound (பவமான) malas are let go. 2538 starts from releasing the nine states from waking; 2834 from becoming Siva so the three malas end. A near-repeat in a distant chapter, it fixes 2538's obscure phrase as part of a stable formula.

2539: in a mind become Siva (சிவமான சிந்தை) the three malas (மும்மலம்) scatter and Siva-knowledge takes their place. 2969: those whose mind has become Siva (சித்தம் சிவமாய்) and who have destroyed the three malas (மலமூன்றும் செற்றவர்) become pure Siva. The same claim in two chapters: the mind becoming Siva and the malas' end are one event.

2541: saying 'my Lord' within night and day, the poet found the Lord cut away strong karma (வல்வினை). Kural 5: the two deeds born of darkness (இருள்சேர் இருவினை) do not cling to those who hold to the Lord's true praise. Both make constant turning to the Lord the thing that frees one from deeds; Tirumular puts it as the Lord's act, the Kural as a fact about the devotee.

source_issues: 2537: the names of the third group of presiding selves (சொலிதையன், பிரசா பத்தியன், விசாந்தன்) are garbled.
2543 line 3 (ஓதுங் கமைமாயே யோரிரண் டோ ரமுத்தி) is corrupt.
2539 line 4 (தவமான மவையாகி) is obscure and may be corrupt.
